_meta.description: Every physical dimension used by TrainTrack comes from this file. Nothing here is guessed — each value names the source it was read from. When a printed piece doesn't fit real track, this is the one file to fix.
sources: torwan, 'IKEA- & BRIO- & others- compatible train tracks generator', OpenSCAD source, GitHub mirror of Thingiverse thing:5598668: https://github.com/torwanbukaj/ikea-brio-others-compatible-train-tracks-generator/blob/master/src/train_tracks_generator.scad (Thingiverse itself and MakerWorld were both unreachable from this build environment's network policy, so the GitHub mirror of the same author's repo was used instead)
CavemanDesigns BRIO track customizer, MakerWorld model 1099116 — NOT YET consulted; blocked by network policy, see note below
_meta.note_on_makerworld: The task asked for dimensions from both torwan's OpenSCAD generator and CavemanDesigns' MakerWorld customizer. This sandbox's network policy blocks both thingiverse.com and makerworld.com outright (confirmed: proxy returns 403 on the CONNECT tunnel, not a site-side error). torwan's generator happens to have a GitHub mirror, so its numbers are real and sourced. CavemanDesigns' customizer does not appear to have an accessible mirror, so Phase 1 relies on torwan's numbers alone. Phase 2a (bundling the 91 pre-made STLs) will need the actual CavemanDesigns files, which will have to be fetched some other way — ask the user to download and hand them over, or open up network access to makerworld.com.

widthMm.source: track_width, scad line 39. Comment: 'Track dimensions (based on original IKEA Lillabo and BRIO tracks)'

wellDepthMm.source: track_well_depth, scad line 41 (depth of the groove down the centre of the rail)

wellSpacingMm.source: track_well_spacing, scad line 44 (centre-to-centre spacing of the two grooves)

peg._comment: The male connector, called 'plug' in the source. Every piece needs at least one of these to connect to a socket.

radiusMm.source: brio_track_plug_radius, scad line 65, marked '(do not change)'

socket._comment: The female connector, called 'nest' in the source.

radiusMm.source: brio_track_nest_radius, scad line 72, marked '(do not change)'

lengthMm.source: scad file header comment, line 20-21: 'Standard lengths of the Brio straight tracks (without a plug): 145mm.' This is the only length the source calls out as the Brio standard, so it's used as the full-size straight.

DERIVED, not directly sourced. The .scad file gives no explicit 'half straight' length. This is half of pieces.straight.lengthMm (145mm / 2). The source's own pre-generated example files do use a halving pattern for straights (straight100mm / straight50mm / straight25mm in pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/), which supports halving as a reasonable approach, but this specific number has not been checked against a real half-straight piece. If you have one, measure it with calipers and correct this value.

radiusMm.source: scad line 18-19 comment: 'Arc parameters used in J'adore system... 45deg, inner radius 86mm'. Corroborated by the author's own pre-generated file pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_arc45deg_r86_b_NP.stl, which uses r86 for the actual Brio-folder curve.

switchY._comment: A symmetric Y-turnout: one common end, splitting into a left and a right branch, each the same curve as curve45.

legRadiusMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_switch_l45deg_r86mmN_r45deg_r86mmN_cN_b.stl — filename decodes as left leg 45deg/r86mm/nest-ended, right leg 45deg/r86mm/nest-ended, common end nest, grooves on both sides

commonGender.source: same file: common end is 'N' (nest = socket)

legGender.source: same file: both leg ends are 'N' (nest = socket)

crossing4._comment: Two straight arms crossing at 90 degrees, each arm peg-ended on one side and socket-ended on the other.

armLengthMm.source: pre-generated_parts_stl/brio/train_tracks_brio_intersect_90deg_100mmNP_100mmNP_b.stl — both arms 100mm, both NP (one nest end, one plug end), 90 degree crossing

loopClosure._comment: These are not physical measurements — they're UX tolerances chosen per the project brief, which notes that real BRIO track flexes 2-3mm at the Vario joins. Tune these here if closure detection feels too strict or too loose.

positionToleranceMm.note: slightly more generous than the 2-3mm of real joint flex, so genuine closures aren't missed

headingToleranceDeg.note: allows for the same flex expressed as a small angular error
